chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ib, from Abu Ubayda Al-Hadda', from Suwayr ibn Abu Fakhta, who said: I heard Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) narrating in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), saying: My father narrated to me that he heard his father, Ali ibn Abu Talib (peace be upon him), narrating to the people.

He said: When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will resurrect the people from their graves in isolation, beardless, hairless, and bald, on a single plain. Light will drive them, and darkness will gather them, until they stop at the hurdle of the Gathering. Some will climb upon others, crowding beneath it, and will be prevented from passing. Their breathing will become heavy, their sweat will increase, their affairs will constrict them, their noise will intensify, and their voices will rise. He said: This is the first terror from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection.

He said: Then the Compeller (Al-Jabbar), Blessed and Exalted, will look down upon them from above His Throne, in the shade of the Angels. He will command one of the Angels to call out to them: 'O assembly of creatures! Be silent and listen to the Caller of the Compeller.' He said: The last of them will hear it just as the first of them hears it. He said: At that, their voices will break, their gazes will become humble, their hearts will tremble, and their hearts will be seized with fear. They will raise their heads toward the direction of the voice, hastening to the Caller. He said: At that moment, the disbeliever will say, 'This is a difficult day.'

He said: Then the Compeller, Mighty and Majestic, the Just Judge, will look down upon them and say: 'I am Allah; there is no god but I. I am the Just Judge who does no injustice. Today I judge between you with My justice and equity. No one will be wronged in My presence today. Today I take for the weak from the strong their due right, and for the owner of the grievance, I take retaliation for the grievance from the good deeds and the sins. I reward for the gifts. And no one will pass this hurdle today in My presence who is an oppressor, or to whom a grievance is owed, except if the owner waives that grievance, and I reward him for it and take it for him at the accounting. So cling to one another, O creatures, and seek your grievances from those who oppressed you in the world, and I am a witness for you against them, and sufficient am I as a witness.'

He said: So they recognize each other and cling to one another. No one remains who has a grievance or a right against another except that he clings to him for it. He said: So they remain as long as Allah wills. Their condition becomes severe, their sweat increases, their grief intensifies, and their voices rise with intense noise. So they wish for a way out from it by leaving their grievances with their owners.

He said: And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, observes their struggle, so a caller calls out from the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, making the last of them hear as he makes the first of them hear: 'O assembly of creatures! Be silent to the Caller of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, and listen. Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to you: I am the Bestower. If you wish to forgive each other, then forgive each other; and if you do not forgive each other, I will take your grievances for you.'

He said: So they rejoice at that due to the severity of their struggle, the narrowness of their path, and their crowding. He said: So some of them forgive their grievances, hoping to be freed from what they are in, and some remain, saying: 'O Lord, our grievances are greater than we can forgive.'

He said: So a caller calls out from beside the Throne: 'Where is Rizwan, the keeper of the Gardens, the Gardens of Firdaws?' He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commands him to bring up from Firdaws a castle of silver, with whatever is in it of buildings and servants. He said: He brings it up to them, and on the outskirts of the castle are the handmaidens and the servants.

He said: So a caller calls out from the presence of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'O assembly of creatures! Raise your heads and look at this castle.' He said: So they raise their heads, and each one of them wishes for it.
He said: So a caller calls out from the presence of Allah, Exalted: 'O assembly of creatures! This is for every one who forgives a believer.' He said: So they all forgive, except for a few.

He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'No oppressor will pass to My Paradise today, and no one to whom a grievance is owed among the Muslims will pass to My Fire until he takes it from him at the accounting. O creatures! Prepare yourselves for the accounting.'

He said: Then their way is cleared, and they proceed to the hurdle, some pushing others, until they reach the plain. And the Compeller, Blessed and Exalted, is upon the Throne. The registers have been spread out, the scales set up, and the Prophets and the Martyrs are present, and they are the Imams. Each Imam testifies over the people of his era that he stood among them by the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and called them to the way of Allah.

He said: Then a man from Quraish said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, if a believing man has a grievance against a disbelieving man, what does he take from the disbeliever, while he is from the people of the Fire?' He said: So Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Bad deeds are removed from the Muslim in proportion to what he has against the disbeliever. The disbeliever is punished by them along with his punishment for his disbelief, a punishment in proportion to the grievance the Muslim has against him.'

He said: The Quraishi said to him: 'And if the grievance is for a Muslim against a Muslim, how is his grievance taken from the Muslim?' He said: 'Good deeds are taken for the oppressed from the oppressor in proportion to the right of the oppressed, and they are added to the good deeds of the oppressed.'

He said: The Quraishi said to him: 'And if the oppressor has no good deeds?' He said: 'If the oppressor has no good deeds, then the oppressed has bad deeds. Bad deeds are taken from the oppressed and added to the bad deeds of the oppressor.'

key_terms.الْجَبَّارُ: The Compeller (one of the names of Allah)
key_terms.عَقَبَةُ الْمَحْشَرِ: The hurdle of the Gathering, a place of congestion on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.مَظْلِمَةٌ: A grievance or right owed to someone due to oppression

ai.seo_question: How are grievances settled between people on the Day of Resurrection according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi vividly depicts the 'Hurdle of the Gathering' (Al-Aqabah), a unique eschatological bottleneck where humanity is driven by light yet gathered in darkness, symbolizing the transition from worldly chaos to divine accountability. It elaborates on the mechanism of *Qisas* (retribution) and *Sadaqat* (good deeds) for settling interpersonal rights (*Huquq al-Adamiyyin*), highlighting that unresolved grievances prevent entry into Paradise until the oppressed forgives or receives compensation. The narrative underscores the justice of Allah, who personally oversees this process, ensuring that no soul is wronged, and clarifies the distinct outcomes for Muslims and non-Muslims regarding the transfer of sins and merits.
